recent_posts.title: Takeaways from a PyTorch Eng Director at MSL
recent_posts.summary: John Myles White, a former Engineering Director on PyTorch at Meta (MSL), shares candid insights on big tech career dynamics. Key takeaways: promotion culture has become so dominant that engineers ship low-quality or unnecessarily complex software just to hit promo bars; employee bargaining power has significantly weakened post-COVID as the perceived surplus of software engineers (amplified by AI productivity gains) lets management make decisions less favorable to employees; and the best way to avoid these dynamics is to deliberately choose teams that prioritize engineering excellence over promo velocity, even if career progression is slower.

recent_posts.title: MSL Eng Director: Promo Hacking, Industry Shifts, Regrets
recent_posts.summary: John Myles White, former engineering director at Meta's MSL, shares candid reflections on promotion culture at big tech, how the employee-employer power dynamic has shifted industry-wide, and lessons from his career. He describes how promotion-obsessed culture in AI Infra and Monetization led engineers to build intentionally coupled systems and ship work they didn't believe in just to hit promo bars. He contrasts this with PyTorch's craft-focused culture, which held higher standards but slower promotions. John also discusses his background as a Julia core contributor, the R vs Python vs Julia language wars, the importance of statistical rigor in A/B testing, and his biggest career regret: never attending his skip-level's office hours out of fear of wasting their time.

recent_posts.title: Turing Award Winner: Data Abstraction, Dijkstra, Distributed Systems
recent_posts.summary: A podcast interview with Barbara Liskov, Turing Award winner, covering her foundational contributions to computer science. Topics include the 1970s software crisis and her invention of data abstraction, the CLU programming language, the Liskov Substitution Principle, Viewstamped Replication and its equivalence to Paxos, Byzantine fault tolerance, her views on Python's lack of encapsulation, stories about Dijkstra's 'Go To Statement Considered Harmful' letter, and reflections on her career in academia including being rejected from Princeton for being a woman.

recent_posts.title: Mike Stonebraker on Postgres history, MapReduce mistakes, and the future of databases
recent_posts.summary: Mike Stonebraker, Turing Award winner and creator of Ingres and Postgres, shares the history behind building these foundational database systems, explains why he publicly disagreed with Google's MapReduce and eventual consistency approaches (which Google later abandoned with Spanner), and critiques Amazon's proliferation of database services. He discusses his current startup DBOSS, which applies database principles to workflow orchestration and application state management. He also covers the limitations of LLMs for text-to-SQL on real-world data warehouses — where accuracy drops to 0% compared to 80%+ on academic benchmarks — and argues that turning heterogeneous data sources into SQL tables with a query optimizer is the right approach for agentic AI workloads.

recent_posts.title: AWS Distinguished Eng: Learnings From 3000 Incidents And How Engineering Is Changing
recent_posts.summary: Marc Brooker, AWS Distinguished Engineer, shares insights from reading 3,000+ cloud system postmortems, covering what makes great postmortems, why on-call is a powerful learning tool, and how AWS's weekly COE review has been central to its success. He explains why caches can be dangerous in distributed systems due to metastable failures, and how Aurora DSQL was designed to avoid common relational database outage patterns using MVCC and optimistic locking. He also shares his perspective on how AI will reshape software engineering careers, advising junior engineers to focus on understanding customers and problems, and senior engineers to stay hands-on with modern agentic tools. He also advocates for writing as a tool for both scaling expertise and sharpening thinking.

recent_posts.title: Ex-Head of Eng at Instagram: Career Regrets and Learnings
recent_posts.summary: James Everingham, former head of engineering at Instagram, shares his unconventional career journey from being kicked out of college and getting an FBI visit as a teenage hacker, to working at pre-IPO Netscape during the browser wars, leading Instagram Stories development, heading Meta's Libra/Novi cryptocurrency project, and now founding Guild, an AI agent management platform. Key lessons include: building relationships over networking, why small focused teams outperform large ones, the difference between CTO and VP of Engineering roles, thinking about your career like an investment portfolio, and how failure often leads to better opportunities.

recent_posts.title: Why understanding workplace incentives separates high performers from the rest
recent_posts.summary: High performers at companies like Amazon and Meta succeed partly because they understand the incentive structures that govern how work is rewarded. Rather than working on whatever feels important, they focus their energy on what is actually recognized and rewarded. If the incentives at your current company don't align with the work you care about, the practical advice is to find a different team or company rather than trying to change the system. Trying to play the game based on how you think incentives should work — rather than how they actually work — is a path to frustration or failure.

recent_posts.title: The Creator of Kubernetes On Building Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: Brendan Burns, co-creator of Kubernetes, shares the story of building Kubernetes at Google — from convincing leadership with the MapReduce/Hadoop lesson and open source strategy, to hacking together an MVP in under a week. He discusses key technical decisions like loose coupling via control loops, declarative configuration, and centralizing state through etcd and the API server. Burns also covers how the project gained industry adoption by donating to the CNCF, writing democratic governance rules, and giving partners a seat at the design table. He also shares career advice on reserving ~10% of effort for self-directed side projects and the importance of timing in disruptive innovation.

recent_posts.title: Meta Hiring Lead On Behind The Scenes of Senior+ Eng Hiring
recent_posts.summary: A former Meta hiring committee lead and mobile hiring manager shares insider details on how the senior+ engineering hiring process works at Meta. Topics covered include: how hiring committees evaluate candidates, how leveling decisions are made from the first recruiter call through final committee review, what behavioral interviews actually assess (scope, organizational impact, leadership), how to avoid being down-leveled, the difference in expectations from senior to staff to principal, how to negotiate level mid-process, compensation negotiation pitfalls, and common mistakes senior candidates make. The conversation also touches on unethical candidates, the role of referrals, and company-specific tips for OpenAI and Anthropic.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI Codex Tech Lead On How His Career Grew And How He Uses Codex
recent_posts.summary: A long-form podcast transcript interview with Michael Bolin, tech lead for the open source OpenAI Codex repository and former distinguished engineer at Meta. He covers his career journey from Google (Calendar, Closure tools) to Meta (building the Buck build system, Nuclide IDE, Eden virtual filesystem) and finally OpenAI. Key topics include how OpenAI engineers use Codex, the difference between research-led and engineering-led company cultures, lessons learned about influence and conflict at senior engineering levels, and advice on career planning, writing, and starting projects well.
